To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

STN stimulation at a low intensity increases GABA levels in the SN and at a high intensity increases Glu levels, and that STN stimulation-induced dyskinesias are correlated with the increase in Glu levels in SNr.

STN stimulation at an intensity corresponding with the threshold inducing forelimb dyskinetic movements in hemiparkisonian rats increases glutamate levels in the substantia Nigra pars reticulate and that the forelimb dyskenesias are mediated by glutamate.
STN–high frequency stimulation-induced forelimb dystonia is linked to an increase in glutamate levels in the substantia Nigra pars reticula.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neurobiological basis of the effects of subthalamic nucleus stimulation on motor behaviour and the neurochemical correlates of these effects.
the mechanisms underlying the therapeutic effects of subthalamic nucleus high-frequency stimulation (STN– HFS) in Parkinson's disease (PDD).
the mechanisms underlying the therapeutic effect of deep brain stimulation in Parkinson's disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
STN-HFS-induced forelimbdyskinesia is linked to an increase in Glu levels in SNr.
STN–HF stimulation increases Glu levels in both the STN and the SNr, but that the increase in Glu levels in SNr is the most important factor in the induction of STN–HF-induced dyskinesias.
STN–HSF-induced contralateral fore-limb dyskinesia in hemiparkisonian rats is mediated by glutamatergic mechanisms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
STN-HFS-induced forelimbs dyskinesias are linked to an increase in Glu levels in SNr, which is probably due to the direct activation of the STN axons.
STN– HFS-induced forelimbs dyskinesias are linked to an increase in Glu levels in SNr, probably via the activation of STN projections.
STN–HF stimulation increases Glu levels in SNr, and that this increase is correlated with STN–HF-induced contralateral forepaw dyskinesia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
high-frequency stimulation of STN induces an increase in glutamate release in SNr, which is correlated to the appearance of dyskinesia.
STN–HF stimulation-induced forelimb dykinesia in intact or hemi-parkinsonian rats is linked to an increase in glutamate levels in the substantia niger pars reticulat.
the motor effects of high-frequency stimulation of subthalamic nucleus in rats are mediated by glutamate in the SNr.
